title: Personal-data-shaped values under a credential-only scope
summary: Ordinary text containing synthetic personal-data-shaped values (a person's name, an address on the reserved example.invalid domain, a telephone number in the fictional 555-0100 range) and no credential, evaluated under a credential-only scope.
rationale: Personal data and credentials are different populations with different expectations. Under a credential-only scope these values are distractors: they test whether a credential finding fires on an email address, a name or a phone number. They say nothing about whether personal data should be masked, which is a separate profile and population that this repository does not define here. Mixing the two would let a personal-data profile's findings be scored as credential false positives, or a credential-only run be read as personal-data coverage.
unscopedReason: The input holds no credential of any family; the values are personal-data-shaped distractors for the credential scope.

expectation.rationale: Not flagged as a credential. This is a scope statement: the maintainer direction in issue #98 keeps personal-data expectations in a separate population or profile and uses these inputs only to test credential scope. It states no personal-data expectation. Decided 2026-10-04 by the deciding maintainer Milo Kang (GitHub milocosmopolitan): option A adopted as a scope statement (docs/decisions/0019-maintainer-decisions-for-epic-92-review-debt.md, issue #142). This credential-evidence population is scoped to credentials and does not assert PII expectations; personal data is measured in the project's separate PII evaluation (pii-eval) with its own population. Nothing here says PII is out of scope for the project or that such values are harmless. A downstream comparison records whether generic-assignment and PII detection were enabled; this repository can state that requirement but cannot enforce it. Status: decided, awaiting second review; no second reviewer is recorded, so the class stays a labelled draft policy, not a fact. Dissent: none recorded. Would reverse if PII expectations are placed in this population.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
